name: Anterior intrapelvic (modified Stoppa) approach to the acetabulum (periprosthetic)
corridor: Low Pfannenstiel approach through the linea alba behind the pubis into the true pelvis, along the pelvic brim to the quadrilateral surface, protecting the bladder and pelvic vessels

positioning.text: Position supine with a sterile bolster under the knee of the injured leg to relax the psoas and vessels.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the pubic symphysis and a transverse Pfannenstiel line just above it.

incision.text: Make a Pfannenstiel incision above the symphysis and incise the rectus fascia longitudinally along the linea alba.

superficial_interval.text: Retract both rectus bellies laterally, partly detach the medial rectus from the symphysis, and stay in the preperitoneal space while dissecting the bladder off the pelvis.

deep_interval.text: Follow the pelvic brim laterally, identify and control the corona mortis before it is divided, mobilize the obturator neurovascular bundle with a malleable retractor, and elevate the obturator internus and periosteum off the quadrilateral surface with a Cobb elevator.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, rectus fascia and linea alba, rectus abdominis, the preperitoneal space with the bladder, and the inner pelvis and quadrilateral surface.

structures_at_risk.text: The external iliac vein, the corona mortis, the obturator neurovascular bundle, and the bladder are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The retropubic corona mortis and the external iliac vein near the elevators are the danger zones for catastrophic bleeding.

retraction_hazards.text: Keep malleable retractors between the vessels and bone, avoid the external iliac vein with elevators, and protect the bladder with blunt dissection.

exposure.text: Gives excellent visualization of the entire quadrilateral surface, pelvic brim, and pubic symphysis, extendable with a lateral window to the iliac fossa.

limitations.text: The lateral window extension is limited by the L5 nerve root on the anterior ala, and blood loss can be significant.

indications.text: Indicated for ORIF of quadrilateral surface, anterior column, and periprosthetic acetabular fractures.

closure.text: Close the midline rectus and superficial layers protecting the bladder and peritoneum, and consider a subfascial drain given significant blood loss.

complications.text: Complications include major vascular bleeding from the corona mortis or external iliac vein, bladder injury, obturator nerve injury, and hematoma.

procedure_applications.condition: A quadrilateral surface or anterior column acetabular fracture needs direct intrapelvic access
A periprosthetic acetabular fracture requires intrapelvic exposure and buttressing

questions.question: Through what plane does the modified Stoppa approach enter the pelvis?
questions.answer: Through the linea alba, retracting the rectus abdominis and staying preperitoneal.

questions.question: Which surface is best visualized with the anterior intrapelvic approach?
What limits the lateral window extension?
questions.answer: The L5 nerve root on the anterior aspect of the ala.
